chunks: Your Lord is certainly in wait.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that God is 'in wait' (Al-Mirshad)?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the term 'al-Mirṣād' (the watchpost) is interpreted not merely as passive observation but as an active, encompassing surveillance where God monitors the innermost intentions and outward deeds of humanity. This verse underscores the concept of divine justice, reminding believers that no action, however hidden, escapes His knowledge, thereby encouraging constant self-accountability (muḥāsabah) in preparation for the final recompense.
